source: SYNTHETIC scenarios CT-50..CT-63 built from public Vates / XCP-ng / Xen Orchestra web-search summaries (hostnames lab.example, addresses 192.0.2.x). Log lines are approximations of real error names, not copied from real logs; they are not resolved support cases.

templates.title: XCP-ng host: dom0 filesystem full, xapi will not come back after a toolstack restart
templates.issue: Host xcp01 is unreachable in Xen Orchestra. xe commands fail with "Connection refused" and the control-domain disk usage alarm fired earlier.
lines: {s} xcp01 xapi: [error|xcp01.lab.example|3321 ||xapi] Could not write database: No space left on device
{s} xcp01 xcp-ng: Disk Usage for Control Domain on server xcp01.lab.example has reached 98%
{s} xcp01 xe-toolstack-restart: [warning] xapi did not come back after the restart; /var/log is 100% full
templates.cause: Per the forum summaries a full /var/log (or /) stops xapi and logging; one thread needed a host reboot even after space was freed. Typical sources named: SR.scan log spam on the pool master and old guest tools.
resolution: df -h and du -xh /var/log | sort -h | tail to find what filled the partition.
Free the space (rotate/remove oversized logs).
If the log spam came from frequent SR scans on the pool master, lower the rate: xe host-param-set other-config:auto-scan-interval=120 uuid=<host uuid> (forum report).
Restart the toolstack (xe-toolstack-restart; check xe task-list first) or reboot the host if xapi still does not start.

templates.title: XCP-ng pool: member host cannot reach the pool master after a power event
templates.issue: After a power event the member host xcp02 reports that the pool master is unreachable and Xen Orchestra lost the pool. The master xcp01 was rebooted.
lines: {s} xcp02 xapi: [error|xcp02.lab.example|88 ||xapi] Unable to contact the pool master xcp01.lab.example (192.0.2.11): connection timed out
{s} xcp02 xapi: [error|xcp02.lab.example|90 ||xapi] Lost contact with the pool master; entering emergency mode
{s} xcp02 xapi: [ warn|xcp02.lab.example|91 ||xapi] HOST_IS_SLAVE: this host cannot execute the request, the master is 192.0.2.11
templates.cause: Per the forum/docs summaries: the member cannot reach the coordinator. Community reports resolved it with an emergency network reset on the affected host or on the master; if the master is truly dead a survivor is promoted manually.
resolution: Check whether the master is alive (xapi on xcp01, management bond/VLAN) before promoting anything.
If HA is enabled: xe host-emergency-ha-disable force=true, then xe-toolstack-restart.
Community fix: emergency network reset on the affected host (after a toolstack restart on the master did not help), then reboot the other members once the master is back.

Only if the master is dead: xe pool-emergency-transition-to-master uuid=<host uuid> on a survivor, then xe pool-emergency-reset-master master-address=<new master> on the others; later xe host-forget the old master.

templates.title: XCP-ng HA: hosts self-fence and reboot after a short management-network outage
templates.issue: Hosts in an HA-enabled pool rebooted and their VMs were restarted elsewhere. The network team reports a short switch outage on the management VLAN.
lines: {s} xcp03 xhad: [warning] heartbeat from host xcp01 lost on the management interface (xha)
{s} xcp03 xhad: statefile access failed: heartbeat disk unreachable
{s} xcp03 xhad: Could not join the liveset: the HA daemon could not access the heartbeat disk
{s} xcp03 xhad: host xcp03.lab.example self-fencing: initiating hard reboot
{s} xcp02 xapi: [error|xcp02.lab.example|55 ||xapi] Lost contact with the pool master
templates.cause: Per the docs summary: a host that loses both the network heartbeat (UDP on the management interface) and the storage heartbeat (ha-statefile) within the timeout (default 60 s) treats itself as problematic and does a hard reboot (self-fence).
resolution: Read /var/log/xha.log on each host to see who self-fenced and who asked whom to reboot.
Fix the management network / bond path and confirm every host can reach the heartbeat SR.
Docs recommend at least 3 hosts; with two, a lost link can get hosts fenced.
To stabilise while investigating: xe host-emergency-ha-disable force=true and xe-toolstack-restart; re-enable with xe pool-ha-enable heartbeat-sr-uuid=<sr uuid>.

templates.title: XCP-ng storage: SR almost full, coalesce stuck, then a VM will not start
templates.issue: A VM will not start after a backup job. The NFS storage repository is almost full and backups began failing earlier this week.
lines: {s} xcp01 SM: [21433] Insufficient space on SR 0a1b2c3d-1111-2222-3333-444455556666: SR_BACKEND_FAILURE_44
{s} xcp01 SMGC: [30112] Unable to coalesce 8f7e6d5c: no space to leaf-coalesce, the SR is full
{s} xcp01 SM: [22001] Raising exception: the snapshot chain is too long (SR_BACKEND_FAILURE_109)
{s} xcp01 xapi: [error|xcp01.lab.example|7001 ||xenops] Failed to start the VM app01: HVM boot failed (the VDI cannot be activated, the SR has no free space)
templates.cause: Per the summaries: coalesce (which frees snapshot space) runs after a snapshot is deleted and can fail when the SR lacks free space, which keeps the SR full and lets VDI chains grow; SR_BACKEND_FAILURE_44 means insufficient space. The VM failing to start is the downstream symptom.
resolution: Free space on the SR first: move VMs/disks to another SR (also forces a coalesce) or delete old snapshots, keeping the base and latest.
Rescan the SR to restart the garbage collector; shut the VMs down before rescanning for a better chance of offline coalesce (user report).
Keep roughly 30% free (XO docs summary); thin-provisioned local ext is more forgiving than thick LVM (Vates staff in a thread).
Then start the VM and review backup schedules that created the snapshots.

templates.title: XCP-ng / XO: delta backups skipped to protect a long VDI chain, coalesce timing out
templates.issue: Delta backups of one VM fail or are skipped. Xen Orchestra reports an unhealthy VDI chain and the SR Advanced tab shows a growing "VDI to coalesce" count.
lines: {s} xcp01 SMGC: [4411] Exception while coalescing VDI 11aa22bb: leaf-coalesce timed out
{s} xcp01 SM: [4502] Raising exception: the snapshot chain is too long (SR_BACKEND_FAILURE_109)
{s} xo01 xo-server[771]: 2026-03-10T09:30:01.000Z xo:backups:worker WARN Backup skipped to protect VDI chain: unhealthy VDI chain on SR nfs-sr01
templates.cause: Per the XO docs summary: XCP-ng caps a VHD chain at 30 elements; the error is a protection and a stuck coalesce is the usual cause. A corrupted VDI can stop the garbage collector (Vates engineer in a thread).
resolution: Check the "VDI to coalesce" count on the SR Advanced tab in XO; if it does not fall over time, grep /var/log/SMlog for exceptions and UNDO LEAF-COALESCE.
ps axf | grep vhd shows whether a coalesce is running; rescan the SR to trigger one.
As a last resort migrate the VM disks to another SR to force a coalesce (XO docs).
A 8.3 leaf-coalesce timeout workaround (LIVE_LEAF_COALESCE_* in cleanup.py) exists in a forum thread but is unofficial; back up first.

templates.title: XCP-ng storage: iSCSI SR will not re-attach after a host reboot
templates.issue: After a host reboot the iSCSI storage repository shows as unplugged and the VMs on it will not start. Plugging the PBD fails.
lines: {s} xcp02 xapi: [error|xcp02.lab.example|120 ||xapi] PBD_PLUG_FAILED: the SR iscsi-sr01 could not be attached
{s} xcp02 SM: [8812] iscsiadm login failed: iSCSI login to 192.0.2.50:3260 timed out
{s} xcp02 SM: [8812] SR is not available: /dev/disk/by-scsid/360000000000000000e00000000010001 does not exist
{s} xcp02 kernel: nfs: server 192.0.2.60 not responding, timed out
templates.cause: Per the summaries no single cause: an iSCSI login/discovery problem (CHAP), a missing /dev/disk/by-scsid device, a hung iscsid, stale NFS mounts, or damaged LVM metadata on a local drive.
resolution: Run xe pbd-plug while watching xensource.log and SMlog.
iSCSI: check iscsiadm -m session, run sendtargets discovery first (it made pbd-plug work once, but the failure returned at every reboot), check whether iscsid is hung.
NFS: unmount the stale path then reconnect; consider hard mount options.
The iSCSI-after-reboot case in the GitHub issue had no confirmed permanent fix in the search summary.

templates.title: XCP-ng VM: a 16 GB VM will not start although the host seems to have free RAM
templates.issue: Starting a large VM on host xcp02 from Xen Orchestra fails with a "not enough free memory" error although the host seems to have free RAM.
lines: {s} xcp02 xapi: [error|xcp02.lab.example|2201 ||xapi] VM.start failed: HOST_NOT_ENOUGH_FREE_MEMORY (required 17179869184, available 12884901888)
{s} xcp02 xapi: [error|xcp02.lab.example|2201 ||xapi] Unable to start the VM db01: not enough host memory
templates.cause: Per the summaries: the memory is already committed (dynamic-max of all running VMs plus dom0), or state is stale after migrations; a toolstack restart fixed one case.
resolution: Compare xe host-list params=memory-free with xe vm-compute-maximum-memory for the VM.
Restart the toolstack (or reboot the host) and retry; consider static memory instead of a dynamic range.
On a smaller second host, dom0 memory also reduces what a 16 GB VM can use.

templates.title: XCP-ng VM: live storage migration of a busy VM fails with MIRROR_FAILED
templates.issue: Live migration (with storage) of a large, write-heavy database VM fails after many hours and Xen Orchestra reports MIRROR_FAILED.
lines: {s} xcp01 xapi: [error|xcp01.lab.example|9100 ||xapi] Storage migration: MIRROR_FAILED, the block mirror could not keep up with the writes of the VM
templates.cause: Per the forum summary (Vates CEO): a live storage migration replicates blocks while the VM runs; if the VM writes faster than the mirror copies, the migration fails.
resolution: Use warm migration for very large or write-heavy VMs (suggested in the thread).
Read /var/log/xensource.log on the source host for the underlying error.
A VM left looking running after the failure: xe vm-reset-powerstate or a toolstack restart (other threads).

templates.title: XCP-ng update: Rolling Pool Update stops on the second host (yum error, evacuation blocked)
templates.issue: A Rolling Pool Update started from Xen Orchestra stopped on the second host. The task is stuck and yum reports errors.
lines: {s} xcp02 yum: Cannot retrieve repository metadata (repomd.xml) for repository xcp-ng-updates: HTTP Error 500
{s} xcp02 yum: Transaction check error: incomplete transactions found
{s} xcp01 xapi: [error|xcp01.lab.example|4400 ||xapi] host.evacuate failed: CANNOT_EVACUATE_HOST (VM app02 cannot be migrated: HOST_NOT_ENOUGH_FREE_MEMORY)
templates.cause: Per the summaries: repository mirror HTTP 500 errors, stale or incomplete yum transactions, backups running during the RPU, and, with HA enabled, HOST_NOT_ENOUGH_FREE_MEMORY during evacuation.
resolution: Clean up incomplete yum transactions and run yum clean all, then update again.
Disable HA and scheduled backups/replication before a rolling pool update.
Manual fallback from forum staff: on each host yum update with the xcp-ng-base and xcp-ng-updates repos, migrate VMs away, reboot, repeat.
CANNOT_EVACUATE_HOST caused by CPU features: shut the VM down and boot it again.

templates.title: Xen Orchestra: scheduled delta backups to an NFS remote fail with VDI_IO_ERROR
templates.issue: Scheduled delta backups from Xen Orchestra to an NFS remote fail every night with VDI_IO_ERROR (Device I/O errors).
lines: {s} xo01 xo-server[771]: 2026-03-10T02:14:09.512Z xo:backups:worker ERROR Backup job nightly-delta failed: VDI_IO_ERROR(Device I/O errors)
{s} xo01 xo-server[771]: 2026-03-10T02:14:10.002Z xo:backups:worker WARN remote nfs-backup01 was disconnected (ESTALE) during the export
{s} xcp01 SM: [5521] VDI_IO_ERROR: reading the VHD of VM db01 failed
templates.cause: Per the XO docs summary: VDI_IO_ERROR comes from the host (dom0), not XO; the host could not read the disk during the HTTP export. Named causes: corrupted VDI or a race during snapshots, a too-slow SR, a long job timeout with a slow remote.
resolution: grep -i error /var/log/SMlog on the host for coalesce or VDI corruption.
Check the job timeout and whether jobs overlap.
For an NFS remote a forum thread suggests a hard mount or adjusted soft timeout/retries (the pipe to the remote closed early and left a partial VHD).

templates.title: Xen Orchestra cannot connect to a pool after its host certificate was replaced (TLS error)
templates.issue: After the certificate on the pool master was replaced, Xen Orchestra shows the pool as disconnected with a TLS error.
lines: {s} xo01 xo-server[771]: 2026-03-10T09:45:11.002Z xo:xo-mixins:xen-servers WARN server 192.0.2.21 connection failed: DEPTH_ZERO_SELF_SIGNED_CERT
{s} xo01 xo-server[771]: 2026-03-10T09:45:41.002Z xo:xo-mixins:xen-servers WARN server 192.0.2.21 connection failed: UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE
templates.cause: Per the summaries: since a 5.8.x release XO refuses to connect to a host whose certificate is invalid (self-signed or expired) unless that is explicitly allowed; the XCP-ng hosts own certificates are managed with xe commands on every host of the pool.
resolution: Verify the new certificate, then either install a certificate XO trusts on every pool host or accept it via the warning/toggle in the XO server settings.
Plain HTTP also works but sends all traffic unencrypted.
Expired appliance certificate: regenerate cert.pem/key.pem with openssl and restart xo-server (docs summary).

templates.title: Xen Orchestra from sources: yarn build fails (node version / native module)
templates.issue: After pulling the latest Xen Orchestra sources, yarn build fails and xo-server does not start.
lines: {s} xo01 xo-install[1201]: error xo-server: The engine "node" is incompatible with this module. Expected version ">=14.5". Got "12.20.2"
{s} xo01 xo-install[1201]: error Found incompatible module.
{s} xo01 xo-install[1201]: gyp ERR! build error
templates.cause: Per the search summaries: the node version does not satisfy the module engine requirement (the example in the summary was Expected ">=14.5", Got "12.20.2"), or native modules fail to compile on an unsupported node.
resolution: Install a node version that satisfies the engine requirement named in the error.
Clean rebuild per the docs: remove node_modules, run yarn, then yarn build.
If a recent commit broke the build, check out a known-good commit (issue report).

templates.title: XOA update fails: updater cannot reach xen-orchestra.com (TLS-intercepting proxy)
templates.issue: Updating the Xen Orchestra Appliance from the Updates page fails. A transparent proxy was recently introduced.
lines: {s} xoa xoa-updater[412]: ERROR unable to reach xen-orchestra.com: self signed certificate in certificate chain
{s} xoa xoa-updater[412]: ERROR upgrade failed, see xoa check
templates.cause: Per the XO docs summary: proxies often break the updater with SSL/TLS errors; other named causes are a corrupted or missing package, no access to xen-orchestra.com and nodejs.org on 443, and a missing registration.
resolution: Run xoa check and journalctl -u xoa-updater -f -n 50 while reproducing.
Allow the proxy to pass xen-orchestra.com and nodejs.org untouched, or (lower security) set NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 in /etc/xo-appliance/env and restart xoa-updater.
Delete /var/lib/xoa-updater/update.json and run xoa-updater --upgrade for a fresh download.

templates.title: Xen Orchestra: update and nightly backups fail with ENOSPC (appliance or remote out of space)
templates.issue: Updating Xen Orchestra fails with "ENOSPC: no space left on device" and the nightly backup job starts failing as well.
lines: {s} xo01 xo-install[1301]: error ENOSPC: no space left on device, write
{s} xo01 xo-server[771]: 2026-03-10T09:26:40.000Z xo:backups:worker ERROR Backup job nightly failed: ENOSPC: no space left on device, write
{s} xo01 xo-server[771]: 2026-03-10T09:26:50.000Z xo:backups:worker ERROR remote nfs-backup01 is full
templates.cause: Only the thread titles were seen in search results (an XO update failing with ENOSPC; a backup error although space seemed available); the article text was not read, so no documented cause is claimed.
resolution: Generic check, not taken from the cited threads: df -h on the XO appliance and on the backup remote, free space, then rerun the failed update or job.
